# CANDIDATE: VOL_COMPRESSION_ORB_BREAK_SHORT

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis
When intraday volatility contracts (ATR narrowing) inside the opening range, a subsequent break of the OR with expanding volume often leads to a mean‑reversion move opposite the break direction. This edge exists because volatility contraction indicates indecision and liquidity absorption, while a volume‑surge break signals trapped opposite‑side traders who must exit, creating a counter‑trend snapback.

## Mechanism
Compute 14‑period ATR on 5‑min bars; if ATR over the last 3 bars ≤ 80% of its 20‑bar average (volatility compression) and price is inside the OR (between OR high and low), wait for a 5‑min bar that closes outside the OR (above OR high for short bias) with volume ≥ 2× the 20‑bar average. Enter short at the close of that bar. Exit shape: Initial stop at the opposite OR boundary (OR low for short) plus 0.25×ATR; target 1:1.5 risk‑reward; if price reaches 1R, trail stop with a 2×ATR chandelier. Regime hint: Best when VIX > 20 (higher volatility environment) and time after 10:00 ET; avoid low VIX (<12) where compression is less predictive.
